newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: JUDGE SAYS MARADONA MANAGER MIDDLEMAN IN DRUG RING.
newsitem.headline: JUDGE SAYS MARADONA MANAGER MIDDLEMAN IN DRUG RING.

text.p: The Argentine judge who indicted soccer star Diego Maradona's manager for dealing in cocaine said on Friday he believed Guillermo Coppola was just a middleman in a major drug-smuggling organisation.
"We're only halfway into our investigation into this drug-trafficking network," Judge Hernan Bernasconi told reporters. "My impression is that Coppola is middle-level."

Arrested two weeks ago after police found a pound (500 grams) of cocaine in a flower pot at his home, Coppola was charged on Thursday with possessing drugs for sale. He remains in custody and could face up to 20 years in prison.

The silver-haired, bronzed 49-year-old says the drugs were planted. He told the judge that after he left his home during a party a few days before the raid Maradona and three women partied there until late the next day.

Bernasconi said it was "important and necessary to call certain people to give evidence: for example, Maradona." The 36-year-old player, who has confessed to a drug habit, will give evidence to a Buenos Aires judge next week.

Maradona was said to be distraught at Coppola's arrest and threatened this week to uncover "hidden dark political and economic interests" behind his friend's prosecution. But the hero of Argentina's 1986 World Cup title backed down on Thursday, expressing through his lawyers his "trust in the justice system and especially Judge Hernan Bernasconi."
Once the world's most expensive player, Maradona's career has faded since a 15-month drugs ban after the U.S. World Cup. He has not played for Buenos Aires' Boca Juniors since August.
Many blame Coppola for Maradona's drug habit, which put him in a Swiss clinic for 10 days last month. Days later he went berserk in a Spanish hotel and smashed up the lobby.
The case is embarrassing the government. Coppola visited President Carlos Menem with Maradona and was a friend of his late son and his private secretary.

But Menem told local radio he believed the case showed the integrity of Argentina's much-maligned justice system. "If that is Judge Bernasconi's decision, we must accept it and of course all those indicted have the right to appeal," he said.

Maradona's brother-in-law, Gabriel Esposito, ex-soccer player Alberto Tarantini and his girlfriend were also arrested but are being sentenced only to drug rehabilitation. Three other men arrested with Coppola have been indicted.
